clue.text: Question on examination paper — “What gas circulates here?”

indicators.note: here points back at the words already written in the clue, so the letters sit inside them
something that circulates goes round, so the run of letters is read the other way round

blocks.note: the tail of question, all of on and the start of examination

explanation.surface: An exam paper on chemistry asks students to name a gas that is circulating in the room.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a question set in an exam, and its own opening words answer it once read backwards: questiON ON EXamination, reversed, spells XENON.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is one of the noble elements, a heavy inert substance found in tiny traces in the air.

clue.text: Nagging wife can make it happen after a kiss

indicators.note: can make suggests the letters are used as raw material to build something different
after says the rearranged letters follow the other piece, so they go second

blocks.note: X is the cross used for a kiss at the end of a letter
the eight letters of the two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A wife who keeps on at her husband gets her way once she has given him a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: After puts the kiss first in the answer, with the rearranged letters following it.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanthippe, the wife of Socrates, was famed as a shrew, so her name stands for any scolding spouse.

clue.text: Christmas present the Spanish give

blocks.note: the present moment is now
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Christmas gift that Spanish people hand over.
explanation.walkthrough: Christmas present reads as a gift, but present is the time now and Christmas alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowel is an old spelling of Noel, the French-derived word for the Yuletide festival.

clue.text: Parsimony of composer wearing cape

indicators.note: a garment that is worn goes round its wearer, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness
Thomas Arne, the English composer of Rule, Britannia

explanation.surface: A composer known for meanness is spotted in a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: Wearing reads as the composer having the cape on, but the cape word is the outside piece: Arne goes inside ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Near can mean stingy or tight-fisted, so nearness is meanness with money.

clue.text: Fantastic claim — wish is realised

indicators.note: a thing realised is made real in a new form, so the letters are rebuilt into another word

blocks.note: the two words supply all nine letters

explanation.surface: Someone makes a far-fetched claim and then the wish behind it comes true.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic in its sense of fanciful or capricious matches playfully odd, the meaning of whimsical.

clue.text: Wash in stir

blocks.note: first meaning: the trail of disturbed water behind a boat
second meaning: to rouse or come out of sleep

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests stirring something into the laundry; wash is the water left behind a vessel and stir means to rouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's wake is the wash it leaves behind, and to wake is to stir from slumber.

clue.text: Concerned with sheep gathering as a whole

blocks.note: to be in something is to be involved or concerned with it
a teg is a sheep in its second year
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: Someone worried about sheep being rounded up all together.
explanation.walkthrough: TEG, a young sheep, is a crossword favourite worth remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: Integrally means as an essential part of a complete thing, taken whole rather than in pieces.

clue.text: Area controlled by military escort, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the word is only one possible arrangement, inviting another ordering

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A zone run by soldiers, who may be providing an armed escort.
explanation.walkthrough: Military escort looks like a phrase, but military belongs to the definition and escort alone is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In army usage a sector is a zone of operations assigned to a particular unit.

clue.text: Bloke joining a bishop and a novice in the bush

blocks.note: a chap is a man
taken as written
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
a as written, and L for learner

explanation.surface: A man teams up with a bishop and a trainee out in the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on British cars, hence a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaparral is dense scrubland of the American south-west, so it is a stretch of bush.

clue.text: It's lawful to walk

definitions.note: read as the two words leg it

blocks.note: first meaning: legitimate, in slang form
second meaning

explanation.surface: Someone reassures us that strolling here is permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words for the second meaning: leg it is slang for going on foot or running off.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is short slang for legitimate, meaning legal or above board.

clue.text: Game in which you'll find many trainers

definitions.text: in which you'll find many trainers

blocks.note: first meaning: a card game of the stops family

blocks.clueFragment: in which you'll find many trainers
blocks.note: second meaning: the Suffolk town that is the headquarters of British horse racing

explanation.surface: A sports game where plenty of coaches, or running shoes, turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Trainers suggest coaches or sports shoes, but here they are racehorse trainers: Newmarket in Suffolk, England, has more racing stables than anywhere in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is both a gambling card game played with a layout of cards and the English town famous for its racing stables.

clue.text: Loud noise from Scots group at midnight

indicators.note: mid- names the middle of the word night, so only its centre letter is kept

blocks.note: a clan is a Scottish family group
the middle letter of night

explanation.surface: A Highland family makes a racket in the middle of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing metallic sound, such as a bell or a dropped pan makes.

clue.text: Maritime industry out west using tugs

indicators.note: out tells us the following letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: hunting whales at sea
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A seafaring business in the western ocean relies on tugboats.
explanation.walkthrough: Tugs look like tugboats, which suits the maritime picture, but here they are pulls or heaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To hale is an old form of haul, so haling means pulling or dragging, giving strong pulls.

clue.text: I grant no dispensation in the dark

indicators.note: a dispensation is an arrangement or ordering of things, so the letters are set out in a new order

blocks.note: all eight letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A church official refuses to grant an exemption without explaining why.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark is an idiom for lacking knowledge or information about something, unaware.

clue.text: Tacks into unoccupied area in slow motion

indicators.note: into puts one word inside another rather than beside it

blocks.note: empty room is space
tacks are small nails

explanation.surface: Someone tacking a sail slowly into open water.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacks suggests sailing, but here they are small nails, which go after the first letter of space.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail's pace is an idiom for very slow progress, since the creature barely creeps along.

clue.text: Wages cover charitable giving and, on the Continent, a feast

indicators.note: on the Continent tells us to use the European, here German, word rather than the English one
to cover is to go round on all sides, so one word wraps the others

blocks.note: alms are gifts to the poor
und is German for and
wages are pay

explanation.surface: Workers' pay includes donations to charity, and in Europe a banquet too.
explanation.walkthrough: Wages go round both the charity word and the German one.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm Sunday, the Sunday before Easter, is a Christian festival, and feast is the church word for one.

clue.text: Seem hurt by order to speed up

blocks.note: to look a certain way is to seem it
to smart is to sting or hurt

explanation.surface: Someone appears upset at being told to get a move on.
explanation.definitionFit: Look smart is a British command meaning hurry up, be quick about it.

clue.text: Catch 6 on the way back

indicators.note: going on the way back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the answer to 6 down is sector, which is a part

explanation.surface: Someone catches a number six bus on the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is a cross-reference to 6 down, sector, which you must turn into a synonym before reading it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch an animal is to trap it, and a catch on a door is also a trap of sorts.

clue.text: Flower providing cover for bird and rats

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece that covers another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: a poppy is a red flower
a cock is a male bird

explanation.surface: A plant gives shelter to a bird and some rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: Rats looks like more animals for the scene, but it is the exclamation Rats!, meaning nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats! is a dismissive exclamation like Poppycock!, both meaning rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Mobius strip is not so controversial

definitions.note: a cryptic description, not a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a Möbius strip, a loop with a half twist, famously has only one surface
second meaning: an issue with arguments on both sides

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle is said to be less divisive than people think.
explanation.walkthrough: Not so controversial looks like one phrase; split after so: the strip is not so, and controversial is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A controversial question has opposing camps, so it is two-sided, while a Möbius band has only one face.

clue.text: By the sound of it, took in island

indicators.note: this tells us to go by how a word is pronounced, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: took in food means ate, said the British way to rhyme with eight

explanation.surface: Someone apparently visited, or swallowed, an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Many British speakers say ate as eight, which is how an eyot, also spelt ait, is pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small island in a river, especially the Thames.

clue.text: Bed-linen given prisoner who's admitted “I shall escape"

indicators.note: someone who has admitted a visitor has let them inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: POW is a prisoner of war
contracted to I'll
to slip away is to escape

explanation.surface: A captive who vows to break out is handed bedsheets, perhaps for a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillowslip is a pillowcase, one of the cloth items making up a bed's linen.

clue.text: Result — torn coat

indicators.note: something torn is ripped apart, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The outcome of a scuffle is a ripped overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long loose overcoat, often belted, named after the Irish province.

clue.text: Show to be deprived of record in first place

indicators.note: in first place says this piece comes at the front of the answer

blocks.note: a disc is a gramophone record
to lose something is to be deprived of it

explanation.surface: A show is going to lose its prize-winning record.
explanation.walkthrough: In first place sounds like winning, but it simply puts the record word at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something hidden is to reveal it, which is what disclose means.

clue.text: Beautiful girl featured in boring commercial

blocks.note: dry means dull
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A pretty model appears in a dull television advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph of Greek myth, nymph being an old term for a lovely young woman.

clue.text: Former Wimbledon champion named top seed

indicators.note: named means said out loud, so the champion counts for how his surname is pronounced

blocks.note: Arthur Ashe won the Wimbledon men's singles in 1975
key means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A past tennis winner is announced as the number one seed.
explanation.walkthrough: Top seed belongs to tennis, but seed alone is the definition. Ashe's surname is said exactly like the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash key is the winged fruit of the ash tree, which carries its seed.

clue.text: Record held by Kipling's python for a long time

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

blocks.note: Kaa is the python in Kipling's Jungle Book
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Kipling's snake keeps hold of an album for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist cosmology a kalpa is an aeon, a cycle lasting billions of years.

clue.text: Broadcast schedule is upset

indicators.note: in a down answer, set upside down means the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: to time something is to schedule it

explanation.surface: The television listings have been thrown into disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are plain synonyms for sending out a signal or radio waves, as a transmitter does.

clue.text: It raises a point still outstanding

indicators.note: read as out-standing, one word stands outside the other

blocks.note: still and yet both mean even now
taken as written
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone brings up an unresolved issue.
explanation.walkthrough: It raises looks like a person raising a point, but the it is the leavening in bread dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast makes dough rise by producing gas, so it is the thing that raises bread.

clue.text: Bad trouble about chasing a marine creature

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word surrounds another
a chaser follows behind, so this piece comes after the other

blocks.note: taken as written
RM is a Royal Marine
ado is fuss or bother
ill means bad

explanation.surface: A dangerous sea creature in pursuit of something causes real trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Marine creature looks like a sea animal, but marine is wordplay and creature alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an American mammal with a bony armoured shell, an animal and so a creature.

clue.text: Cleaner put chap off

blocks.note: put, read with off at the end of the clue, gives the verb put off
a gent is a gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady discourages a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Put off means deter and chap means gent; the setter has tucked chap inside the phrase, but the pieces simply run one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a washing agent, a substance used for cleaning.

clue.text: Had lush imbibed?

blocks.note: had shortens to 'd, as in I'd
lush and rank both describe overgrown vegetation

explanation.surface: Did the drunkard have a drink?
explanation.walkthrough: Lush looks like a heavy drinker, but here it is luxuriant growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbibed is a formal past tense for taking in liquid, which is what drank means.
